title: Vendor Performance Analysis
summary: A procurement and inventory analysis workflow connecting sales, purchases, pricing, invoices, and vendor performance.
problem: Procurement decisions become difficult when sales, purchasing, pricing, and invoices remain disconnected.
solution: An analytical workflow connects those datasets to make vendor performance and inventory questions inspectable.
architecture: Case-study context: Procurement questions become difficult when sales, purchasing, pricing, invoices, and vendor information remain disconnected across separate tables.
Data assembly: Python and pandas establish a repeatable cleaning and joining path for the operational tables. Components: Python, pandas.
Query layer: SQL and SQLite make the analytical questions explicit and keep the working dataset inspectable. Components: SQL, SQLite, Jupyter.
Decision views: Data visualization turns the joined data into vendor and inventory observations that can be discussed. Components: data visualization.
Python and pandas ingest, clean, and join sales, purchase, price, vendor, and invoice data.
SQL and SQLite make the analytical tables and vendor/inventory questions inspectable; the README describes ingestion and summary-generation scripts.
Jupyter and data visualizations support analysis of profitability and operational efficiency.
outcomes: Procurement analysis workflow connecting sales, purchases, pricing, invoices, and vendor performance.
Focused on the analysis workflow and its questions rather than unsupported dataset-volume claims.
Kept the output compact enough to inspect as a portfolio case study.
The portfolio describes a procurement analysis workflow connecting sales, purchasing, pricing, invoices, and vendor performance.
